WRITING SUB-TEST: MEDICINE

TIME ALLOWED:                        READING TIME: 5 MINUTES
                                     WRITING TIME: 40 MINUTES

Read the case notes below and complete the writing task which follows.


Notes​:

You are a doctor at Celtic Way GP Practice. You are examining a 73-year-old assisted-living resident
who believes he has worsening arthritis



Patient Details:    Sydney Cherry (73)

D.O.B​:             17.04.1947

Address​:           Oakwood Senior Living Community Flats, 12 Queensbury Gardens, Birmingham



Medical History:    2007 Osteoarthritis (OA) − mostly of shoulder and fingers

                    2013 Hypertension (HT) – well-controlled

                    Irritable Bowel Syndrome – 10 years, intermittent

                    Sciatica – intermittent

Medications​:       Co-tenidone 12.5mg daily

                    Panadol Osteo (extended-release paracetamol) 2 tablets t.d.s.

Physiotherapy​:     8 sessions for the management of sciatica (2016)

                    6 sessions for the management of knee pain (March 2019)



Social Background​:

                    Lives in own flat in an assisted-living complex (on-call nurse and duty warden)

                    Very active community member (tennis, chess, gardening, social club treasurer)

                    Has a dog (Bobby). Regularly takes on walks 45 mins (+)

                    Currently learning Japanese

                    Civil Engineer (retired)

    Treatment record:
 
2
     03/03/2019       Pt. experiencing increasing pain on walking / imbalance

                      No joint swelling/redness (subjective)

                      No recent injury to knee

                      L knee − some pain on walking, not nearly as bad as R

                      ↓ ROM of R knee due to pain / tender to pressure - joint

     Treatment:       Referral for X-ray of L knee, blood tests

                      Naproxen 250mg b.d.


     27/03/19         X-ray: Evidence of severe OA in R knee - osteophytes and loss of joint space

                      Patella appears normal / No evidence of fractures

                      Blood: FBW, UEC (normal)

     Assessment:      Likely worsening OA

                      Pt. keen to arrange physiotherapy

                      ↑Analgesia


     07/07/19​:       ↑ Pain in R knee on walking - increasing over last 12 months.

                      Now quite severe − not relieved by regular Panadol Osteo or physio / exercises

                      Pain can even occur at rest after a long walk.

                      Pt. worried about losing his active lifestyle and “growing old and useless.”

                      Referral for surgical consultation - ? knee joint replacement

     Presenting complaint

     25/10/19

                      Pt. has considered advice from consultant (Mrs Antonia Guardia) and spoken to
                      family and friends, and despite concern has agreed to have surgery.

                      Arthroplasty​ date confirmed: 20th November 2019

                      Admission to hospital confirmed: 19th November 2019



Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter of transfer that the patient will take with him to Dr James
Robins, Orthopaedic Ward Doctor. Address the letter to Dr Robins, Head of Orthopaedic Ward, St Peter’s Hospital,
Birmingham.

In your
answer:

      ● Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences

      ● Do not use note form

       ● Use letter format
